exercises.title: Current through a resistor
exercises.brief: A 12 V supply drives a 470 Ω resistor. Work out the current that flows through it, in milliamps.

exercises.title: Power in a resistor
exercises.brief: A 5 V supply is connected to a 1 kΩ resistor. How much power does the resistor turn into heat, in milliwatts?

exercises.title: Resistor for an LED
exercises.brief: A red LED drops 2.0 V and should run at 15 mA from a 9 V supply. What value of series resistor do you need, in ohms?

exercises.title: Current at a junction
exercises.brief: 1.2 A arrives at a junction and splits into two branches. One branch takes 450 mA. How much goes down the other branch, in milliamps?

exercises.title: Two resistors in parallel
exercises.brief: Two resistors of 3 kΩ and 6 kΩ sit in parallel. What is the equivalent resistance, in ohms?

exercises.title: Voltage around a loop
exercises.brief: A 15 V source drives a loop with a 220 Ω and a 330 Ω resistor in series. What is the voltage across the 330 Ω resistor?

exercises.title: Divider output
exercises.brief: A 10 kΩ and a 15 kΩ resistor form a divider across a 12 V supply. Take the output across the 15 kΩ resistor. What is the output voltage?

exercises.title: Design a divider
exercises.brief: You need 2.5 V from a 10 V supply. Put a 20 kΩ resistor on top. What should the bottom resistor be, in ohms?

exercises.title: Why the output sags
exercises.brief: Your divider gives the right voltage with nothing attached, but the voltage drops as soon as you connect the circuit. Explain why, and say what you would add to fix it.

exercises.title: The RC time constant
exercises.brief: A 10 kΩ resistor and a 22 µF capacitor form an RC circuit. What is the time constant, in milliseconds?

exercises.title: Charging after one time constant
exercises.brief: A capacitor charges through a resistor from a 10 V source. After exactly one time constant, what is the voltage across it, in volts? (Hint: 1 − e⁻¹.)

exercises.title: How long to settle
exercises.brief: A 4.7 kΩ resistor and a 10 µF capacitor make a filter. How many milliseconds does it take to settle to within 1% of the final value? (Use five time constants.)

exercises.title: The RL time constant
exercises.brief: A 100 mH inductor and a 220 Ω resistor form an RL circuit. What is the time constant, in milliseconds?

exercises.title: Energy in the field
exercises.brief: A 50 mH inductor carries 2 A. How much energy is stored in its magnetic field, in millijoules? (E = ½LI².)

exercises.title: The spike when you switch off
exercises.brief: You switch off a coil and the voltage across it spikes to hundreds of volts. Explain what is happening, and say what you would put across the coil to protect the switch.

exercises.title: Cutoff frequency
exercises.brief: An RC low-pass uses a 4.7 kΩ resistor and a 100 nF capacitor. What is its cutoff frequency, in hertz?

exercises.title: Resonant frequency
exercises.brief: A 10 mH inductor and a 100 nF capacitor form a tank circuit. What is the resonant frequency, in kilohertz?

exercises.title: Choosing the filter
exercises.brief: You want to keep a slow sensor signal and strip off fast switching noise on the same wire. Say which kind of filter to use, and what to watch out for when you choose its component values.

exercises.title: Average of a half-wave signal
exercises.brief: A 12 V peak sine wave goes through a single diode. What is the average (DC) voltage after the diode, in volts? (Vpeak ÷ π.)

exercises.title: Ripple on a smoothed supply
exercises.brief: A supply delivers 50 mA at 100 Hz into a smoothing capacitor. What ripple voltage do you get, in millivolts, with a 2200 µF capacitor? (Ripple = I ÷ (f·C).)

exercises.title: Why the forward voltage moves
exercises.brief: The same diode does not have the same forward voltage at every current. Explain why, and say what happens to a diode that is driven in reverse beyond its breakdown voltage.

exercises.title: Current through a lit LED
exercises.brief: A blue LED drops 3.2 V and has a 470 Ω resistor from a 5 V supply. How much current flows, in milliamps?

exercises.title: Why white is brighter than green
exercises.brief: Two LEDs use the same power, but the white one looks brighter. Explain what is happening inside the white LED, and say what controls how bright an LED looks.

exercises.title: XOR truth table
exercises.brief: How many rows of a 2-input XOR truth table have the output high?

exercises.title: Push the bubble through
exercises.brief: A NAND gate has an inversion bubble on its output. Describe how you would rewrite it using De Morgan’s theorem, and say which other gate it becomes.

exercises.title: Mixing logic families
exercises.brief: You connect an old TTL chip to a modern CMOS chip. Explain what goes wrong at the voltage levels, and say what the gap between the low and high thresholds is called.

exercises.title: Half adder output
exercises.brief: A half adder adds A = 1 and B = 1. What is the carry out, as 0 or 1?

exercises.title: Full adder with a carry in
exercises.brief: A full adder adds A = 1, B = 1 and a carry in of 1. What is the sum bit, as 0 or 1?

exercises.title: How many select lines
exercises.brief: You want a multiplexer that can pick one of eight inputs. Explain how many select lines it needs and why, and mention one practical limit that comes with the design.

exercises.title: Setting a latch
exercises.brief: An SR latch is set (S = 1, R = 0). What is Q, as 0 or 1?

exercises.title: Why the clock edge
exercises.brief: Explain why a D flip-flop only takes its new value on the clock edge and not continuously, and say what would go wrong in a design where it changed continuously.

exercises.title: Counting up
exercises.brief: A 4-bit counter starts at 0 and is clocked once per second. What is its value after 9 seconds, as a decimal number?

exercises.title: Sampling rate
exercises.brief: You need to capture a signal with components up to 8 kHz. What is the minimum sampling rate, in kilohertz, according to the sampling theorem?

exercises.title: Why the filter has to come first
exercises.brief: Explain what aliasing is, why an anti-aliasing filter has to be placed before the converter rather than after it, and say what filter type is used.

exercises.title: The noise you cannot see
exercises.brief: Your analogue reading is noisy and drifts. Name two different sources of that noise, and say what you would change about the layout or the ground return to reduce it.

exercises.title: Loading on a line
exercises.brief: A logic output drives a 50 Ω input. What percentage of the output voltage actually appears at the input, if the output impedance is 5 Ω?

exercises.title: Build a divider
exercises.brief: Build a voltage divider: a battery across node 1, a resistor from node 1 to node 2, and a resistor from node 2 to ground. Set the two resistors to 1 kΩ each, then check that the output node sits at half the supply.

exercises.title: Build an RC circuit
exercises.brief: Build an RC charging circuit: a battery across node 1, a resistor from node 1 to node 2, and a capacitor from node 2 to ground. Run the simulation and watch the voltage at node 2 rise towards the supply.

exercises.title: Build an LED circuit
exercises.brief: Build an LED circuit: a battery across node 1, a resistor from node 1 to node 2, and an LED from node 2 to ground. Run the simulation and read the current through the LED.

exercises.title: Set a precision bias point
exercises.brief: Use the supplied 6 V battery and two resistors: node 1 to 2, then 2 to ground. Design for 4 V at node 2 (±0.04 V) with 2 mA source current (±0.05 mA). Your ratio must also give 2 V when the checker changes only the supply to 3 V.

exercises.title: Calibrate under load
exercises.brief: Use two resistors from 1 to 2 and 2 to ground. On 6 V design for 3.6 V unloaded and 3.0 V when an instrument connects 6 kΩ from node 2 to ground (±0.04 V). The checker attaches the instrument temporarily. Build just the divider.

exercises.title: Null a two-arm bridge
exercises.brief: Connect two divider arms from node 1 to ground with midpoints at nodes 2 and 3. On a 6 V supply both midpoints must read 4 V, their differential must be within 0.01 V of zero, and total supply current must be 3 mA (±0.05 mA). Multiple resistor combinations work.
